clue.text: A modern language?

parts.note: the question mark warns that this is not French or Spanish but a computer coding language used to build web pages

explanation.surface: A puzzle about which tongue counts as up-to-date.
explanation.walkthrough: You expect a spoken modern language, but the answer is the markup language that web pages are written in.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypertext Markup Language is a recent invention, a code for laying out web pages, so it is a modern language of a sort.

clue.text: In a flash, neutron moves lower in part of an atom

indicators.note: in a down clue, lower means further down the column, so the letter for neutron shifts later in the word

parts.note: done in a flash means done at once, pronto
N is the symbol for a neutron

explanation.surface: A physics picture: a neutron suddenly dropping within an atom.
explanation.walkthrough: In PRONTO the first N shifts down past TO, giving PROTON. The neutron of the surface is only a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A positively charged particle in the nucleus is one of the components of every atom.

clue.text: Woman's relative mostly supported by daughter alone

indicators.note: in a down clue, being supported means sitting on top of what follows

parts.note: Una is a woman's name; with the possessive it gives UNAS

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a sister is a family relative

explanation.surface: A family scene: some woman's sibling propped up by a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims SISTER to SISTE; in a down clue 'supported by' puts D underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something alone means doing it without help from anyone else.

clue.text: Gold and special metal found in Texas

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
tin is a metal

explanation.surface: Prospectors striking gold and some rare metal in the Lone Star State.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the capital city of Texas, which also suits the puzzle's theme of car makes.
explanation.definitionFit: The state capital of Texas is a city that is found within that state.

clue.text: Surrey town to provide meat

parts.note: to cater is to provide food and drink
ham is a cured meat

explanation.surface: A town in Surrey offering to supply the meat for an event.
explanation.definitionFit: Caterham is a town in Surrey, a county south of London; it also names a sports-car maker.

clue.text: American actor wants gold for country

indicators.note: wants here means lacks, so the letters for gold are missing

parts.note: Martin Landau was an American film actor
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A Hollywood actor wanting gold in exchange for a whole nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wants' means lacks, not desires: Martin Landau loses AU.
explanation.definitionFit: A land is a nation or country, as in a foreign land.

clue.text: Extra hearing transposes the limits of ultrasound

indicators.note: the outer letters of the word ultrasound are swapped, one end letter standing in for the other

parts.note: an audition is a hearing, a trial performance

explanation.surface: An extra hearing test involving ultrasound.
explanation.walkthrough: The first and last letters of 'ultrasound' are U and D; changing the U of AUDITION to D makes ADDITION.
explanation.definitionFit: An addition is something extra, added on to what was already there.

clue.text: Flatten headless, evil-tempered dwarf

indicators.note: headless means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: a troll is a surly creature of folklore, often dwarfish

explanation.surface: An instruction to squash a nasty, decapitated little creature.
explanation.definitionFit: To roll something, like pastry or a lawn, is to make it flat.

clue.text: Sailor, soldier and university lecturer start to attack spider

parts.note: a tar is an old name for a sailor
a soldier ant is a kind of ant

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A sailor, a soldier and an academic beginning to attack a spider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soldier' is not a member of the army here but a soldier ant.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarantula is a large hairy spider.

clue.text: Sound of distorted dialogue, eg line's split

indicators.note: distorted means the letters are twisted out of their order
split means the named letters part company with the rest

parts.note: taken as written
L is an abbreviation for line; the 's means is

explanation.surface: A sound engineer complaining that garbled dialogue is breaking up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distorted' rearranges DIALOGUE; 'split' removes E, G and L from it, leaving DIAOU to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Audio is recorded or broadcast sound, as opposed to pictures.

clue.text: Lily Savage's debut follows large breakout

indicators.note: follows means the letter comes after the earlier pieces

parts.note: the word reads as break + out: the letters of out broken up and rearranged

indicators.note: a debut is a first appearance, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Lily Savage, the drag act, making a big breakthrough on debut.
explanation.walkthrough: Lily Savage was the drag persona of British comedian Paul O'Grady, but 'Lily' is the definition. 'breakout' splits into an anagram signal and its fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is a water lily, a sacred flower in Asia.

clue.text: On this, exercise is routine drudgery

definitions.meaning: a gym machine with a moving belt you walk or run on
dull work that goes on and on without change

explanation.surface: A gym-goer's view that working out is just tedious routine.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a running machine and, figuratively, a wearisome round of repetitive work.

clue.text: 10 + 10 divided by small number? That's a strain

indicators.note: divided by means split apart by a letter placed inside

parts.note: ten is the number 10 in words
10 written in letters looks like IO

explanation.surface: An arithmetic puzzle: twenty divided by something small, and isn't that a strain?
explanation.walkthrough: The two 10s are read differently: the first as a word, the second as the look-alike letters I and O.
explanation.definitionFit: Tension is stress or strain, whether in a stretched rope or a nervous mind.

clue.text: Least wobbly magnetic unit

indicators.note: wobbly means unsteady, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Describing the steadiest of magnetic measures.
explanation.definitionFit: The tesla is the SI unit of magnetic flux density; it is also an electric car maker.

clue.text: Beatniks somewhat high starting to puff on empty pipes

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the word is kept, here its front half
empty means the middle of the word pipes is removed
on means the next piece sits after the one before it
the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Beatniks getting a bit high as they puff on pipes with nothing in them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' keeps the front half of 'high', HI; 'empty' takes the middle letter out of 'pipes', leaving PIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatniks and their 1960s successors are loosely grouped as counter-culture types, bohemian dropouts.

clue.text: For each goal, obtain authorisation

parts.note: per means for each, as in per person
a mission is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: Every target needs official sign-off first.
explanation.definitionFit: Permission is formal consent, an authorisation to do something.

clue.text: Animal over 50 shot to pieces

indicators.note: over here means placed across, so the numeral sits inside the scrambled letters
shot to pieces means broken up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: An animal more than fifty years old, blasted apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to pieces' rearranges SHOT to SOTH, and L goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloth is a slow-moving South American mammal.

clue.text: Upright film detective

definitions.meaning: an upright column or pole, such as the stem of a pillar
John ..., the private eye of the 1971 film and its sequels

explanation.definitionFit: A shaft is a long upright rod or column, and also the surname of a famous screen private eye.

clue.text: President covers up extremely important case

indicators.note: covers means surrounds the other piece

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, US president

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: vital means extremely important

explanation.surface: A president hushing up a matter of great importance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the synonym for 'extremely important'. 'case' is not a legal matter but grammar; 'extremely' belongs to the synonym, not a letter pick.
explanation.definitionFit: In Latin grammar the ablative is one of the noun cases, expressing means or separation.

clue.text: Hit action man? No sweat

indicators.note: no means the following piece is absent

parts.note: Rambo is the action hero of the Sylvester Stallone films
BO is body odour, the smell of sweat

explanation.surface: A child's toy soldier, Action Man, striking without breaking a sweat.
explanation.walkthrough: Action Man is a British boy's toy soldier; here the action man is Rambo, minus BO.
explanation.definitionFit: To ram something is to hit it hard, as a ship rams another.

clue.text: Old star trained anew, winning first of Grammies

indicators.note: winning means taking in, so the other letter goes inside
anew means made again in a new form, so the letters are reordered
first of means the initial letter is used

explanation.surface: An ageing pop star, retrained, winning a Grammy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old star' sounds like a has-been musician but is astronomy.
explanation.definitionFit: A red giant is a large cool star late in its life, so it is an ageing star.

clue.text: Drummer from Dorking playing without drum kit, initially

indicators.note: playing means the letters are put into play in a new order
without means some letters are left out of the mix
initially means the first letters of the words are taken

explanation.surface: A drummer from a Surrey town gigging without his kit.
explanation.walkthrough: Dorking is a town in Surrey. 'without' removes D and K (initials of 'drum kit') from DORKING; 'playing' rearranges the rest, ORING.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringo Starr was the drummer of the Beatles.

clue.text: Suggested being fooled from Germany to Albania?

indicators.note: from marks the letters that are taken away to be swapped
to marks the letters that are put in their place

parts.note: deluded means fooled or misled
DE is the international code for Germany
AL is the international code for Albania

explanation.surface: Someone hinting at being duped on a trip between Germany and Albania.
explanation.walkthrough: The country codes (as on cars or web addresses) replace each other: DE becomes AL.
explanation.definitionFit: To allude to something is to suggest or hint at it indirectly.

clue.text: Take a trick over 1 heart to win

indicators.note: over here means spread across, so the card play encloses the numeral

parts.note: to trump is to take a trick in cards with a trump suit
I is the Roman numeral for 1
H is the abbreviation for heart in cards

explanation.surface: Bridge advice: take the trick by playing a heart.
explanation.definitionFit: To triumph is to win or prevail.

clue.text: Non-drinkers receive insignificant comments online

indicators.note: receive means take the other piece inside

parts.note: TTs are teetotallers, people who drink no alcohol
wee means small, insignificant

explanation.surface: Teetotallers getting trivial remarks posted online.
explanation.definitionFit: Short messages posted on the social network formerly called Twitter are its comments online.

clue.text: Former tabloid editor's male body part

parts.note: an organ is a part of the body, such as the heart

explanation.surface: A cheeky remark about a newspaper editor's anatomy.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Piers Morgan edited the News of the World and the Daily Mirror, both British tabloids.

clue.text: Morning's start with brewed coffee — it's to do with the weather

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter
brewed means stewed into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word it joins the mixture; the 's is the verb is linking to the definition

explanation.surface: Morning coffee brewed while checking the weather forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewed' rearranges COFFEE plus IT. Its 's only links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Met Office is Britain's national weather forecasting service, so everything it does concerns the weather.

clue.text: About band from the '90s making comeback: one only works for money

indicators.note: making a comeback means coming back, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: C is circa, about
R.E.M. was a US rock band popular in the 1990s

explanation.surface: A '90s band staging a reunion purely for the cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making comeback' reverses C plus REM.
explanation.definitionFit: A merc, short for mercenary, is a soldier who fights only for pay.

clue.text: President once was able to buy off a Fed

indicators.note: off means the following letters are taken away

parts.note: to afford something is to be able to buy it
F stands for federal, as in a Fed

explanation.surface: A past president bribing a federal agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buy off' looks like bribery, but 'off' removes A and F from AFFORD.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerald Ford was US president in the 1970s.

clue.text: Peering in closer, I found a little line in print

indicators.note: peering in means looking within the following words

explanation.surface: Looking closely at printed text and spotting a tiny line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peering in' points inside 'closer, I found'.
explanation.definitionFit: A serif is the small stroke at the end of a letter's main lines in some typefaces.

clue.text: Eat no food in banquet that lacks energy

indicators.note: lacks means the following letter is missing

parts.note: a feast is a banquet

explanation.surface: Starving yourself at a lacklustre banquet.
explanation.definitionFit: To fast is to abstain from eating.

clue.text: Dog starting to retrieve cricket balls

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: an over in cricket is a set of six balls bowled

explanation.surface: A dog beginning to fetch cricket balls.
explanation.definitionFit: Rover is a traditional name for a pet dog, and roving means wandering.

clue.text: Alan is not revising subjects

indicators.note: revising means reworking, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A student called Alan skipping his revision subjects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subjects' is not school topics but citizens of a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Nationals are citizens of a country, its subjects.
